utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Mr. Tieger, has the Prosecution filed the response that I referred to last week?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I think we sent a courtesy copy at about - Mr. Reid would know the precise time - around 5.00 on Friday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Pack, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: General, I want to start with your involvement in the Srebrenica operations, 1995. You've been interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor on three occasions; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You maintained originally that you didn't enter Srebrenica town, that you were never physically inside the town. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I said that I entered Srebrenica to inform General Krstic of the line reached by our units.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me just remind you of your second interview with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: 65 ter 25369, please. This is dated April 2000, 3rd of April, 2000, and if you could go, please, to page 9. I'm afraid it's only in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm going to read it out to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So just at the bottom there. Page 9 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: "Just for the clarity of what you just said, not to make confusion of with what you told us in your previous statement, in the first time-frame you get us, you said, 'I was in Srebrenica and Zepa.' You meant the area of Srebrenica or the Srebrenica town and recall what you told us first time because I am cautioning you on this answer, do you mean Srebrenica area or Srebrenica town?" And you answered: "Operation." Are you looking at your statement -- if you could look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And it's the last two pages of this interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: In the B/C/S it's over the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just at the top in the B/C/S at line 3 is just what I read out and I'm just going to read you what follows, you can see for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And we can now go over in the English, please, to page 10. And I'll just continue reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So you answer to that question: "Operation." And then you say -- and then the question: "Because you told us you never went to Srebrenica town last time." And you answer: "My unit was in Viogor. It is not to refer to the town of Srebrenica, but on the operation." Answer [sic]: "Yeah ... but ... "Q. Just to make it precise, because you made that point very clear last time that you did not at any moment enter the town? "A. My unit never entered ... "Q. Nor did you personally do that? "A. The unit never entered. "Q. And yourself? "A. I only passed by but only ... passing by when I went to Viogor. "Q. Uh-huh, and what date was that? "A. On the 12th ... but when I was heading for Viogor for ... "Q. Our recollection is that you told us you went from Bratunac to ... "A. We went Suceska, Milici, for Zepa ... heading to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So you -- let me precise on this, sorry to give it up on interview which was terminated, you say that 12 July you went through Srebrenica town but coming from where and going towards where? "A. No, through the town there is a certain road that" -- Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not receiving interpretation nor can the witness see the text. So we need the next page and the interpreters are unable to interpret because it's being read too fast and then they can't see where it's being read from.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Perhaps the interpreters could let me know if they're able to read the transcript which is written on -- which is on e-court now in B/C/S. We can turn over just now to the following page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since we --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Which would be the last page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We do not know where the interpretation stopped, probably you have to start over again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And speak to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And read slow, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm unclear if the interpreters got any of it. Let me start at the beginning. So we go back, please, to page 9 of the English and to the preceding page in B/C/S, please. Thank you. Now, does everyone have line 3 in B/C/S and in English, line 24? So we'll go again. "Just for the clarity of what you just said, not to make confusion of with what you told us in your previous statement. In the first time-frame you get us, you said, 'I was in Srebrenica and Zepa.' You meant the area of Srebrenica or the," and if we can go over in the English, please, "Srebrenica town and recall what you told us first time because I am cautioning you on this answer, do you mean Srebrenica area or Srebrenica town? "A. Operation. "Q. Because you told us you never went to Srebrenica town last time. "A. My unit was in Viogor. It is not refer to the town of Srebrenica, but on the operation. "Q. Yeah ... but ... just to make it precise, because you made that point very clear last time that you did not at any moment enter the town. "A. My unit never entered ... "Q. Nor did you personally do that? "A. The unit never entered. "Q. And yourself? "A. I only passed by but only ... passing by when I went to Viogor. "Q. Uh-huh, and what date was that? "A. On the 12th ... but was when I was heading for Viogor ... "Q. Our recollection is that you told us you went from Bratunac to Sase ..." And then we can go over in the B/C/S to page 11. Continuing: "We head Suceska, Milici, for Zepa ... heading to Zepa. "Q. So, you ... so ... let me precise on this ... sorry to give it up on interview which was terminated, you say that 12th July you went through Srebrenica town, but coming from where and going towards where? "A. No, through the town, there is a certain road that passes nearby Srebrenica in the vicinity, which is in vicinity of Srebrenica that leads to Viogor. "Q. Okay, so we are back on your initial statement when you claimed that you never went physically inside Srebrenica town, am I correct? "A. No, not at all. "Q. Nor did you go to Potocari? "A. /not translated/. "Q. So, we are clear now."

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So you originally said to -- in interview by the OTP, that you didn't enter Srebrenica town and you now do accept, don't you, that you were in the town personally on the 11th of July; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Firstly, I wish to say that this wasn't an operation. This was, above all, a battle. The operation is conducted by the corps. At this level, we're talking brigade units which engage in battles and combat. So let's, first of all, say that there was extensive combat here for the separation of the two enclaves. As far as my presence in Srebrenica is concerned, I think that in a third version, after a long period of time, I clarified that I arrived in Srebrenica on the 9th to visit my units. I brought them presents, cigarettes, some food. General Krstic asked that I should remain and lead the mentioned combat group. Because of the casualties that we had on the axis of the Zvornik Brigade. I remained there, as is stated, until the 13th of July, when we left --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can you pause a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to the Zepa area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just a question about the 11th of July. You now accept, don't you, that you entered -- personally you entered Srebrenica town on the 11th of July; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I went outside of Srebrenica when NATO bombing took place, this, in order for me to see what the situation was like with the command where Generals Mladic and Krstic were. I also went there to inform General Krstic of the line reached by my unit, to inform him how far my unit had advanced --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You've seen --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- after that I went back to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You've seen the now well-known video of you in Srebrenica town on the 11th of July shaking General Mladic's hand; yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's on the edge of Srebrenica, on the way into Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm not going to put it up but the reference is page 39 of e-court at Exhibit P4202.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You can show it as well, but after that I went back to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's move on. In your interviews with the OTP and in your statement, you have maintained that you only took up duties as Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps in August; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took up the duty of the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps on the 8th of August. I think that you have my record of hand-over of duty between me and the commander of the Birac Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And that's your evidence, is it --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and if you don't, we'll find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And that's your evidence, that you were not appointed Drina Corps Chief of Staff before then? You're absolutely certain?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certain? I can show you the document indicating the hand-over of document between Colonel Vlasic who took over my brigade on the 6th of August, that was when I handed over my brigade in the presence of General Krstic. And on the 8th of August, I took up the duty of the Chief of Staff. And an annex to the order is the statement of the assistant in charge of mobilisation and organisation affairs and the brigade commander --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, let's --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and if you want me to submit it here, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's look at the document that you have referred to in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Which is 65 ter 02604 which is now Exhibit D3889.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just in fairness to have it up briefly to look at it and then I'm going to show you some other documents.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document, a record on the hand-over of duty or the transfer of duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And this is when -- your evidence is that you weren't appointed as Drina Corps Chief of Staff before then; yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So can we look at P04485.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is the document dated 13 July by which you were appointed Chief of Staff; right? You've seen that before? Yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. I did see the document. However, this document does not mean that one has actually taken over a duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we have P03044.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is the document you can see whereby you're appointed as Drina Chief of Staff -- Drina Corps Chief of Staff with effect from the 15th of July, 1995, you can see that at the bottom, "appointed as of 15 July 1992," yes? This is the presidential decree?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes? And on the same day your successor was appointed, wasn't he, the successor in the position of commander of the Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: We'll go to the next document, please, 65 ter 25375.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is the document, and you can see it's signed by Minister Milan Ninkovic, dated 14th July 1995, identifies Ljubomir Vlacic as the new commander appointed as of 15 July 1995 to the commander of the 1st Birac Infantry Brigade. You'd agree that that's what this document states, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. However, Madam, this doesn't mean that both I and Colonel Vlacic took up duty. First of all, Colonel Vlacic could not have been transferred duty by me when I was in Zepa until the 2nd of July. It was only on the 2nd of July that I arrived in the area of responsibility of the Birac Brigade so it was impossible to do it. Now, between the 2nd and the 6th, the transfer of duty took place. In order for one to transfer duties that are this responsible to someone, you need to first inform the future commander of his duties and obligations. When I handed over duty on the 6th, there was a ceremony where General Krstic, as the brigade commander, addressed those present; and it was after that that I officially handed over duty. A decree does not automatically mean that duty was taken up. I could have taken up that duty five months later --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You agree, don't you --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and that's a fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- that a brigade couldn't have two commanders at the same time?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade had its commander until the 6th, that was Colonel Andric, and as of the 6th it was Colonel Vlacic. However, what you are unaware of is that as of the 9th of June until the 2nd July I was in the Zepa battle-field and I was being replaced by Lazic Milenko. He was standing in for me. Since Colonel Vlacic was my Chief of Staff and deputy -- was in the area of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Help me with this: You would agree, wouldn't you, that once Vlacic is signing off on command reports and orders as the commander of the Birac Brigade, we can probably draw the conclusion that he was, in fact, working and operating as the commander for the Birac Brigade; right? That he'd taken up his duties; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took up duty officially on the 6th and he signed document. Previously, he would sign on behalf of the commander or for the commander. I was still the commander but somebody was signing for the commander or on behalf of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: 65 ter 25403, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Help me with this document, please. It's dated the 22nd of July. It's from the commander, 1st Birac Infantry Brigade and it's signed -- type-signed Lieutenant-Colonel Ljubomir Vlacic, 22nd July.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. Since I was absent, that's the 22nd of July, I was absent at the time and he could not have signed it as commander. I don't think there is his signature here. It must have been some of his desk officers who wrote it, it's a regular combat report, and you would have duty officers who would automatically write him down as commander on the basis of information they had but he wasn't. In order to clarify this quandary, if I may ask you to take the statement by the brigade commander and by the assistant for mobilisation and organisation affairs, this statement was certified --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let -- let me just deal --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and handed over to the court. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- with something else.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: 65 ter 25404, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General Andric --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- if your explanation is a correct one, this document has something wrong. According to your explanation, your name should have appeared and Mr. Vlacic should have signed it for you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, Mr. President, Colonel Vlacic wasn't at the brigade at the time either. He was engaged in combat of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and Colonel Lazic was standing in for him. Did he put it automatically? I'm telling you under full responsibility that a decree does not automatically mean transfer of duty and that I handed over my duty on the 6th of August and received my duties at the Drina Corps on the 9th of August, and there are documents issued by senior levels that attest to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter 25403 admitted, first, before I go on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you identify the 65 ter numbers that you are tendering?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 25403, the one that I've just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Only --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And if I can also have admitted -- I previously referred to the interview, to three pages in that interview, 65 ter 25369, which I read, and it was pages 9 to 11 of the English. I'd ask also just while I'm dealing with admission to have those three pages admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you're not tendering the other two documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: The other two documents are already exhibited, P03044 is already admitted in evidence as is the prior --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was referring to 65 ter 2604.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to have admitted, please, 25369, just the three pages; 25375, which is the document appointing Vlacic to the position of commander; and 25403, which is the document I've just shown the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. And we would appreciate it if these documents could be tendered at the time --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... absolutely, my apology to Mr. Robinson. Let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We'll admit those three documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits P6452 through to Exhibits P6454 respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the Prosecution kindly, do they have this telegram in written form? It's a telegram you cannot see the signature. Perhaps there is an original document with the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm not sure which document -- to which document Dr. Karadzic is referring. 25403, which I've just admitted, I'm using the best document that the Prosecution has. If I can go to the next document in this chain it's 65 ter 25407, please -- I'm sorry, my apologies. 25404. Now, I'm afraid I've only got this in B/C/S at the moment and I would ask that we just look at the B/C/S and obviously we'll arrange for it to be translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: If we can just look, please, just -- you can help us with this. This is a document that's dated, you can at the top, the 25th of July, 1995. And if you look, it's an order from the 1st Birac Brigade? Is that right? The 1st Birac Brigade command, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Dated the 25th of July, yes, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And if we could turn over the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You can see there, can't you, personally signed by the commander, Ljubomir Vlacic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to have that document admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6455, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to add that it's a fact that a signature is there, but someone cannot sign as the brigade commander when the previous brigade commander did not hand-over duty to him. Secondly, I did not see Colonel Vlacic from July 9th until the 2nd of August, so when a duty officer hands over duty in an office, he has to do it with a report, not like this. I mean, how can you hand-over duty over the telephone? Then you should ask him why he signed, but I think that duty was handed over the way I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Could I have, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General Andric, is it not by any chance possible that the take-over ceremony could take place as a formality after actual hand-over had taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A ceremony can take place, but the hand-over of duty between two commanders could not be physically carried out. If I was in Srebrenica on the 9th and from the 13th in Zepa, we only saw each other on the 9th or the 2nd. So you cannot hand-over -- you're not handing over a file, you're handing over a brigade. So I'm responsibly stating that that was so. As for why he signed documents, that is something that I'm seeing now for the first time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You were signing documents, weren't you, as Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps in July; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that it's not clear in the transcript, just like earlier, instead of "August," July was mentioned. But I will clarify that. However, on page 14, line 24, could we please clarify with the witness what is the ninth month and what is the second month. It was the 2nd of August that was mentioned, but the witness needs to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 2nd of August. On the 2nd of August, I arrived in the area of responsibility of my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's what the witness is saying, so obviously he's just making a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you meet Lieutenant-Colonel Vlacic on the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I left Lieutenant-Colonel Vlacic on the 9th of July and I went to Srebrenica on the 9th of July, as I said previously, to tour my combat forces. Then on the 9th, according to the -- pursuant to an order of General Krstic, I remained along the axis of attack of my combat group until the 13th, in the morning, in Srebrenica. From the area of Viogor on the 13th, we continued to march towards Zepa. Until the 9th of -- the 2nd of August, 1995, when on the 2nd of August, together with my combat group, I arrived at Sekovici and there is a written record of this, a TV video record of this. So this is something that can be documented.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to clear up this confusion, please. Can we turn to 65 ter 25402. Now, I'm -- I apologise, we don't yet have a translation again of this document, so in B/C/S only.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me just describe it and perhaps you can agree that I'm describing this document correctly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I forgot to note the previous document will also be marked for identification. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So this document is entitled "Drina Corps command work-plan for August 1995," and you can see that it's dated the 28th of July, 1995. Yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: That's the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we please go to the last page, 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature as yours?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Could you bring back the second page, please -- the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd ask you just to confirm, this is your signature, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Signed as Chief of Staff, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Drina Corps Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Can I look at the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Go back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the Drina Corps command work-plan for August 1995, but it's true that I signed it retroactively after I took up that duty because the operations officer made the plan. When I arrived on the 8th, I signed it. I could not have signed it on the 28th because I was in Zepa. In Zepa, no document was signed because there were no conditions for the document to be brought or for it to be drafted. It was during the combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So your evidence is --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- that this was signed retroactively, that you wouldn't have signed anything as Drina Corps Chief of Staff until 8th of August; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the work-plan for the month of August. In view of the fact that the operations officer prepared the plan when I came -- which should have been signed by the Chief of Staff, Krstic was the Chief of Staff at the time, somebody was supposed to sign it, I signed that plan when I came. That is the monthly work-plan, no order. It's just the work-plan of the Drina Corps command. It's an unimportant, insignificant document in terms of the operation for Srebrenica and Zepa --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So you wouldn't --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it's not important.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You wouldn't have signed anything until the 8th of August, is that right, when you say that you were appointed Chief of Staff; yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you are asking of me, and I'm saying again I was the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps from the 8th of August on and I signed this plan here. Probably I don't remember. It was probably done retroactively. In view of the fact that it's a monthly work-plan, it has no significance. You're trying to convince me the whole time. I'm responsibly telling you when I took up that duty. You cannot take up duty in a forest, I mean without any record, without anything like that. I mean, you're trying to convince me about something that is pointless.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to have that document admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we can [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P6456, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And one last document, please, 65 ter 25405.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: We'll deal with this quickly. Dated the 3rd of August, prior to the date upon which you say you were appointed, type-signed by you, Chief of Staff Drina Corps command, and it's an order, yes? If we turn over the second page in the English we can see the signature. Agreed?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that this is the communications organisation and order of the newly formed Drina Brigade, Drina Corps command. This is a document to organise the communications.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to have that admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6457, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Do you still maintain your denial, General Andric, that you weren't appointed to the Drina Corps position of Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps until August 8th, that you didn't take up duties in July?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I assert that I did not take up my duty then but that I took it up on the 8th of August. And I want to show you the whole time a document, a statement by the assistant for organisation and mobilisation who was responsible and he prepared this, signed it before the court, that that was when I took it up. It's possible that I appeared in the Drina Corps later but not officially.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: We're going to move on. You have told us in your statement - and let me just remind you of the paragraph, 29 - you have told us, and I can summarise what you say, that nobody obstructed Hague Tribunal investigators in the zone of the Drina Corps in their investigation -- in their investigations, for which you were personally thanked. That's what you tell us at paragraph 29 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your evidence is that you would not personally obstruct investigations by the Office of the Prosecutor, is it? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was three times in the offices of The Hague Tribunal when summoned but also when my father died I went even then. And the investigators were very grateful because I did respond. They came numerous times to the corps command area of responsibility while I was the corps commander. I always received them. So it's possible that sometimes I did not, but for the most part I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You had three meetings in 1999 to 2000, early 2000, with Momir Nikolic and others. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Momir Nikolic? I met with quite a number of commanding officers, in view of the fact that the corps area of responsibility was quite large and there was a series of units in the area of responsibility. So whether I met with somebody two, three, four times, once or three or four times, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can I have, please, 65 ter 22350 and it's the last page, please, in the English and also in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I want to remind you of meetings you had with Momir Nikolic in December 1999/early 2000. This is what he says. I'll read it. "I was summoned to an interview by the ICTY in December 1999. Just prior to attending this interview, I was called to a meeting at the Zvornik Brigade Headquarters. I met General Andric, Dragan Jokic, Lazar Ostojic, Dragan Jevtic, and General Miletic there. There were also some civilian lawyers from Belgrade present. "The lawyers instructed us on our legal rights. General Miletic appealed to our patriotism and asked us not to divulge information which would damage the state, and General Andric said we should say as little as possible. After my meeting with the ICTY, I met again with General Andric. The topic of the conversation was the same and he wanted to know if I had spoken about the killings to the ICTY. I was also visited by State Security just prior to my meeting with the ICTY, and was threatened that I should not speak of their involvement. "Several months after the first meeting, I attended again a similar meeting that was held again in the Zvornik Brigade headquarters, with the same individuals including, I think, Dragan Obrenovic, who had been recently summonsed by the ICTY. General Miletic and Andric again told us not to provide any information related to the Srebrenica events to the ICTY." You accept that you told Momir Nikolic and others not to provide any information related to the Srebrenica events to ICTY?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, quite the contrary. I received a document from the Chief of the General Staff to help all of those people who were in any way suspected or were witnesses. And primarily the aid was in the financial sense, material sense, particularly when I asked him and when I told him not to talk about the killing, how could I say that to him when I did not even have information about that. Therefore, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecutor please explain the context in which this document was obtained from Nikolic. Was that in the context of the plea agreement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, that's improper intervention.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you can take that up in your re-examination, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me show you the first page, please, of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we look at page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for information, this is Exhibit D02081.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility of Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Now, this set of meetings, General, this set of meetings and what you said to Momir Nikolic, this reflects, doesn't it, your approach in your dealings with the Office of the Prosecutor, doesn't it? Your approach is to say as little as possible, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that is not true. Quite the contrary. I had a completely different position, that everyone should be held responsible for what they did. I never was in favour of concealing people who inflicted harm, not only to the Muslim population but also who harmed the reputation of their own Serbian people. So that was not my objective. My objective was to provide material assistance pursuant to an order received from the superior command and also professional assistance if necessary. I think that there was one meeting. I don't recall --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your interest --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- any others.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- was to inhibit the investigation of these Srebrenica events, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That was never my goal. I wouldn't have responded to the summons three times, and as commander of the corps, I would not have ordered all of my senior officers to respond also.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your interest has been to lie to the Office of the Prosecutor, hasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Why would I lie.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's go to Zvornik and Vlasenica, please, in 1992. You tell us in your statement that Zvornik municipality was in the zone of responsibility of your brigade from its establishment until the 2nd of June, 1992, and that Vlasenica municipality remained in your zone of responsibility until 16th January 1993. And I'm just summarising your statement at paragraph 2; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You were effective, weren't you, in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Effective, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, let's see what you achieved.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we look at P03055.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is the order you refer to in your witness statement that you say wasn't implemented. It's dated the 28th of May, 1992. And you'd agree that it's signed by you; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And let us just read what you order at paragraph 6. "The moving out of the Muslim population must be organised and co-ordinated with the municipalities through which the moving is carried out. Only women and children can move out, while men fit for military service are to be placed in camps for exchange." This is your order, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You didn't issue an order revoking this order? No?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I issued this order on the 28th of May, when Muslim forces from Kalesija were attacking along the Tuzla-Zvornik axis. So I was in the middle of combat, but that is not reason for me to justify myself, quite the contrary. This order or, better said, information was given to the TO staff in Zvornik for the reason that the TO staff commander did not act pursuant to the order of the 15th of May, 1992, which was an order for defence signed by lieutenant -- by Colonel Tacic. Because he did not place his units under the command of the Birac Brigade. He used the same units wilfully. In order to prevent this wilful conduct, uncontrolled taking of prisoners and so on, I wrote this order because I received certain information before that from people from Zvornik that there were several paramilitary formations there and that they were committing some improper things. They were --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- bringing prisoners out without a judgement and they were liquidating them. But on the 31st, I issued an order in view of the fact that the TO staff did not want to subordinate and place itself under my command. On the 31st, I issued an order of a request nature, where I was asking for the command of the TO staff in Zvornik to participate in co-ordinated action on the Tuzla-Zvornik axis, to send their operative officer in order to organise this co-ordinated action, which means that this order of mine from the 31st proves that this order of the 28th of May was not implemented or carried out --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes. You've addressed --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that much.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- this theory in your statement. Let me just ask you this, you --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Go ahead, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You're aware, aren't you, that within days of your order, between 4- and 5.000 Muslim men, women, and children were forced out of the municipality, loaded onto buses at Djulici by soldiers from various VRS companies and police working together. You're aware of that, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. However, I received information and that's why I issued the order. That's why I issued the second order as well. It is pointless for me to go on explaining. I could go on explaining for two days, but it would still be pointless. The TO staff command did not obey my order. They were not under my subordination. This was stated by the TO staff commander and the president of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik at the special court for war crimes in Belgrade where they were on trial. I appeared there as a witness and I asked them and they confirmed that they never took my order into account. They never obeyed my command. I don't know whether this suffices at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Djulici was in your zone of responsibility before the 2nd of June? Yes? Yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Again, for an umpteenth time I am telling you that the TO staff and its command and the 6th Infantry Battalion were not placed under my command. I was not in command of those units at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You -- let me just tell you what else happened Djulici on -- this is on the 1st of June. Over 700 men, over the age of 16, men, as you say -- wait a second -- men as you describe at paragraph 6 of your order, men who were fit for military service, they were separated from the women and children and they were taken to Karakaj technical school, where they were guarded by soldiers from the Karakaj Company. You're aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know why you are asking me about that again and again. I told you to go to the statements from the special court in Belgrade, where both the TO staff commander and the commander of the 6th Infantry Battalion stated they were not under my command at all. I'm not saying that I didn't sign the order and I can explain why I did it, but, again, it's totally pointless.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's go to P3237, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You'll be familiar with this document. It's from the command of the Eastern Bosnia Corps, your then corps command, and it's dated the 7th of June, 1992, addressed to the Main Staff. Let me just ask, please --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And in the English, can I ask, please, that we go to the second page. We can stay on the same page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And in this report, the Eastern Bosnia Corps in -- on the 7th June 1992 is reporting in paragraph 8: "In the area of Zvornik we have around 500 prisoners, and in the area of Vlasenica around 800." Now, it's right, isn't it, that those 500 prisoners are the prisoners at Karakaj technical school, and the 800, the prisoners at Susica camp which you set up, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to ask the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Mr. Colonel Blagojevic, about that. When it comes to Susica, I believe that there were prisoners, but I believe that there were about 650 of them. Because on the 17th of June, and even before that on the 6th, I drafted a letter which was to be sent to the command of the East Bosnia Corps to deal with the prisoners. And then on the 17th of June, again the commander of the Main Staff ordered that the prisoners should be transferred to Batkovic camp, in Bijeljina, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, we'll come back to Susica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd ask for P05400, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You can see it's another order of the 7th June 1992 --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- from the command of the Eastern Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd ask to go to the page 4 in the English, page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to look, please, at paragraphs 5.7 and 5.8. Let's look at paragraph 5.8. Paragraph 5.7 orders that the Zvornik Brigade continue their ciscenje operations and ensure traffic flow through the Drina River valley. And you at paragraph 5.8, you, the Birac Brigade, same thing at the end there. "At the same time, carry out ciscenje, /mopping up or cleansing/, operations and ensure traffic flow in Drina River valley ..." That's describing ethnic cleansing, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the Zvornik Brigade, not about Birac Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, look -- look at paragraph 5.8, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: It's describing ethnic cleansing, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not ethnic cleansing. No. It's the mopping up of the territory to deal with paramilitary formations, both on the Muslim side as well as on the Serbian side. We had a problem with paramilitary formations in Zvornik. The situation was such that we had to clash with them, and that applied to certain armed groups on the side of the Muslim Crisis Staffs and local units as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, let's sit and look at the areas where you were operating.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: 65 ter 24560, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: In October - we'll have this document up in moment - in October 1993, which is this document here, you gave a report of your brigade's activities since its establishment and that's what this document represents, doesn't it, dated the 30th of October, 1993, from the command of the 1st Birac Infantry Brigade. Yeah? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to focus on Vlasenica municipality. So if we look at page 3 of the English and B/C/S page 3, just at the bottom of the English, bottom two paragraphs in the English. Thank you. And in the B/C/S, it's also the bottom three paragraphs in the B/C/S. It says: "The liberation of the town of Vlasenica on the 21st of April, 1992, saw the start of the combat operations from that area and so in May 1992, we reached the line: Drum - Kula - Jaroblje, this from Piskavica via Alihodzic, Urici and Mesici. "In June 1992 we went further on: Dzemat, Begici, Kuljancici, so that on the 2nd June 1992, having started from Gradina and going via Hrastovac - Pijuk and Jasikovice, we reached the Grobic-Potajnik line. Constant enemy assaults only serve to speed up," and over the page, please in the English, "the shift of our forces forward. By the 4th July, our forces were already along the line the villages of Becirevici - Rogosija - Jasikovac - Potajnik." And if we jump forward, please, to in the English page 7, B/C/S page 7, you describe the areas you liberated in Vlasenica. At the bottom of the English, bottom two -- last-but-one bullet point, "in the territory of the municipality of Vlasenica ..." and in the B/C/S it's the second paragraph. Let me read it. "In the territory of the municipality of Vlasenica, a number of villages were liberated: Piskavica, Alihodzic, Urici, Mesici ..." it goes on. The Gradina feature, and so on, I don't need to read it all out to you. You can see that. These are areas in which units under your command, within your zone of responsibility, were involved in operations, is that right, in 1992? Yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And what this meant, liberating these areas, this meant cleansing these areas of Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. You have to go back to the period of the month of April. Up to the 19th of April, that is. Up to then there was practically no Muslim population in Vlasenica. On the 18th of April, the last official of the Muslim authorities, Izet Redzic accompanied by the president of the Crisis Staff, Mr. Stanic, at his own request was transferred to the territory under the Muslim control. This means that departures were organised throughout the month of April. These villages here that are mentioned in this document, that was a festive moment when the brigade celebrated its anniversary and those villages were in the hands of the enemy, not of the civilian population. The enemy was armed. They had caused a lot of problems, they had inflicted a lot of casualties, and at that time there was an ongoing struggle between the two enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me just --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me remind you --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me ask you some questions about these villages. Drum?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: The evidence in this case is that on the 2nd of June, over 20 male Muslim villagers were executed in Drum by soldiers. You're aware of that; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Soldiers who were supported by an APC. Didn't hear about this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get the reference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you, the area of responsibility of the Birac Brigade during that period of time comprised seven municipalities. The battalions within those municipalities were independent, which means that my battalion commander was fighting on the Vlasenica-Cerska axis. I believe that that was the 5th Battalion. The 1st Battalion was engaged on the Tuzla-Zvornik axis. The 3rd Battalion was engaged on the Sekovici-Kladanj axis. Therefore -- or the Skelani Battalion was engaged in Skelani. I'm reading this the same way you are, and believe me, I don't remember this. I did not participate in all that, but I'm sure that some of my battalion commanders did. I --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Did what --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- can't remember --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- did execute Muslim villagers? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. In the liberation thereof.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get the reference?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, KD --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is implied under the term "execution," and can we get the reference as to where it says that those were executions?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'll provide the references. KDZ603, statement exhibited as P03262 at paragraphs 7 to 23. See also KDZ230. Also Defence witness Mane Djuric, testimony on the 7th of March, T 34970. Those are my references. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Gradina, another village that you liberated. The evidence in this case is that Muslims in the Gradina operations --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what was the date of that? Give me the date?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me ask the question. Muslims in the --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you said -- I can't talk about things without being aware of the date. I have to focus on my answer, but I have to be aware of the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Muslims in the Gradina operations in June 1992 were rounded up and detained, their houses were burned and other villages were burned. That's the evidence is the case. Reference KDZ033 statement, P03227, paras 38 to 43. Are you aware of those operations?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I believe that the army did not participate in those operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: By the end of 1992 you'd been very effective in Vlasenica municipality, hadn't you, General? You'd cleared the territory, virtually all of it, with the exception of this Cerska enclave, of Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said, "General, you were effective," but I can tell you that I was not actually. If you analyse the situation and if we go back to that period, you will see that there were no generals there and that the army or the battalion, rather, did not participate in that. If my memory serves me right, I have information about Gradina, according to which special units or some other TO units were involved in that. No battalion of the Birac Brigade was involved in those operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This was your zone of responsibility, right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that was my area of responsibility; however, in principle, an area of responsibility of a brigade is 10 to 15 kilometres normally, but my zone -- area of responsibility was 160-kilometres wide. That was the core zone or the core area. I don't know which brigade would have been able to control such an area of responsibility. If I'd been able to do that, I'm sure that military experts would think that I was a Napoleon no less.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And you were reporting to your corps on liberating these areas and you well knew, didn't you, you well knew, well understood the aim of the operations that you were carrying out in your zone of responsibility --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- to conquer and clear that territory of Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I believe that this was a speech which was delivered on the anniversary of the brigade. When you deliver a speech of that kind, you want to mobilise your fighters, and you receive information from your subordinate battalion commands as to what they'd done. The operative drafts a speech, and such a speech has to be delivered when things are celebrated. Then you try to raise the morale of their fighters to help them persevere in their struggle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's deal with this document by document. I'd ask for this document to be admitted in evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6458, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And you know and I know that you're referring to the transcript of your speech, 1D09090 - if we could have that up - that you refer to in your witness -- that's exhibited with your witness statement. Let's just look at that speech.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: We don't need to look at the first page in English. If we can look at the second page in the English, please, and the second page in B/C/S. It's just the transcript. Second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is what you say, your speech in Milici: "My favourite applause will be when the Serbian Bosnia is free and it will be when we are all equally involved in that struggle, the Serbian history will show that I can tell you that never" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have an English translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Oh, my apology. I thought it had come up. Yes, there should be one. It's certainly been uploaded because it was provided to us by the Defence. And could we have the second page, please, in both. Thank you. And it's the last paragraph we want to look at. Thank you. "My favourite applause will be when the Serbian Bosnia is free and it will be when we are all equally involved in that struggle, the Serbian history will show, but I can tell you that never in the Serbian history we had such a chance to win. This brigade holds 70 per cent of the territory of SAO Birac compared to the 30 per cent that the enemy holds. According to that, just a little effort is needed to retain those areas and to conquer more, then the President Karadzic can go peacefully to the conference. Otherwise, if we allow the enemy today, tomorrow, until 26th, 27th, to perform what is intended, then I fear that we will allow them to meet its objective. That is why I call you all once more ..." You well understood the aim of the operations that you were carrying out, didn't you, to conquer and clear that territory of Muslims; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you are actually twisting things. This speech was a consequence of the attack of the 28th Division on the Serbian village of Podravanje. On the 24th, 33 civilians were killed on that occasion, 40 went missing, 90 were expelled. The village of Milici and the bauxite mine were under threat. They were of vital significance for Republika Srpska and Bosnia and Herzegovina as a whole. I returned and I asked the representatives of the radio to organise a rally, where I was to appeal to all able-bodied men to come to the front line. And if you listen to the recording of that speech, there were women and children there and I was begging them to appeal to their parents to defend Milici and Republika Srpska. Therefore, who was engaged in operations here? On the 25th, the situation was as it was. The morale was low, there were a lot of casualties. I gathered as many people as I could, even the oldest ones who were not able-bodied, and I set out to try and break through in order to protect villages from Derventa to the bauxite mine. On the 25th, luckily enough, we managed to suppress the enemy although they had inflicted a lot of casualties. What would you expect me to say at that rally? What would you expect, to praise Naser Oric? Of course not. I couldn't after so many casualties and those were not the only casualties. 3 .200 men and about 500 women and children had been killed by the 28th Division, and now you expect me to watch calmly when my fighters and civilians were being killed. This was a speech aimed at mobilising all able-bodied men. On the 26th, in the territory of Vlasenica, the same division attacked from the territory of Rogosija and killed 28 new people so there --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Pause a moment, please --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please wait. 60 people were killed over the period of two days. What was I supposed to do? Applaud? I couldn't applaud.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's focus on Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 19119, please. I just want to locate a few places on the map. This is the map book. I don't know if Your Honours have it with you. It's at page 50 of the hard copy of the map book. And the 65 ter 19119, if we can have that on the screen. It's just a single map of Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Ms. Pack, 19119 has yet to be released.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: My apologies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, line 18, page 35, there is something unclear. The witness's answer was interrupted. Maybe it would be good if the witness was allowed to finish his sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm afraid it's going to have to be enlarged a bit. I hope it shows it better on the screen. Perhaps it can be enlarged just so the surrounding areas are removed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Now, the key -- we can see the key in a moment just so we can get the distances right. Now, this is a map you'd recognise of Vlasenica municipality. Now, the place names are in English but I can read them out to you. You see where the red dot is on the left is Drum village. And just below that with the orange triangle, Susica camp. You see those locations? And if you move to the right, you can see Milici. Yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And if we go upwards -- upwards from Milici we can see at the top of the page Cerska, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And if we go back towards the centre, we can see Gradina?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And if we can just zoom out again, just to get the whole of the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: At the top of the page there, right at the top centre, village Gobilje, you see at the top, above Cerska? Just have a look.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just above that, Gobilje, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Gobilje.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And then finally if we can zoom out and just look at the key.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You can see the key there. 0 to 20 kilometres, that's the distance represented by the line at the bottom left; can you see that? So you can help us with the distance --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: -- the distance from, let's say, Susica camp to Milici, what is about 10, 15 -- 15 kilometres? You're a better judge than me.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Could I have that map admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is this not part of evidence that we have already admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I understand that the map book hasn't been admitted in its entirety, although Your Honours do have it. So each individual map is admitted as we go along, and this one hasn't yet been admitted as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6459, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we take a break if it is convenient?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for half an hour and resume at 11.02.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: We just, before we broke, we were looking at a map of Vlasenica municipality. Vlasenica Battalion was under your command; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: The security officer of the Vlasenica Battalion, Captain Risto Vidovic was under your command; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was under the command of the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Major --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Professionally under the command of the chief of security of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Major Mile Jacimovic was the commander of the Vlasenica Battalion. He was under your command; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can I have P03240? Now, do we also have -- we have it also in English, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is the order, isn't it, by which you set up Susica camp, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order does bear my signature; however, it was not pursuant to this order that I established the camp. If you want an explanation, I can give one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 of this order states: "Set up a camp in Vlasenica ..." Is that Susica camp?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was Susica camp; however, go back to the heading. The command of the brigade of the Serbian Army Birac. The date, 31st May 1992. What does it state in the heading? Security for prisoners, order. I suppose you would have instead here the establishment of camp because first you have to establish something in order to provide security for it. To organise a camp does not equal establish a camp. Organise a camp means organise order, law and order, discipline, whereas setting up, establishing, is when you are forming it. In other words, this order does not relate to the establishment of a camp.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it is in that sense that the English translation is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is an order, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that it is an order that I signed; however, we -- you fail to understand what organise -- organising means and what establishing means.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's go to P03220, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is another document which relates to the camp which you set up, Susica. It's dated the 14th of June, 1992. Paragraph 2 we can see indicates that there are 640 prisoners in the camp; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: There were men, women, and children?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the composition.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You don't know the composition of the camp that you set up, that you're reporting on the numbers of prisoners held in it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're going back to the same issue. I didn't establish the camp. I organised it. Let me explain this for Mr. President here. The camp came into being as a result of the circumstances prevailing, especially in Zvornik, where there were paramilitary formations which arbitrarily took up people such as in Celopek out of schools, work-places, executed, et cetera. According to the information I received, it became clear to me that I had to issue an order to organise the camp and primarily to secure -- to provide for its security, and it was to that effect that I instructed the commander that a POW camp should be set up. The commander made an assessment of it, designated the organs that would be in charge with maintaining law and order in the camp. Now, the brigade command or the battalion command would not be the ones to set up camp. They would designate the areas where people would be assembled pursuant to an order, whereas a camp would be set up pursuant to an instruction from the corps. So as a result of this order, the POWs should be transferred as soon as possible from the areas of combat, in the process they should be disarmed and seized of certain items, to the areas where they would be assembled. And then after they are registered and categorised, they would be transferred to a camp, which is at the level of the corps. So my requests vis-à-vis the superior command - there was several of them - I remember one of the 17th of June where I informed the superior command that we had I think 650 prisoners and that I asked that the matter be resolved as a matter of urgency. Based on my request, the commander of the Main Staff ordered the command of the East Bosnia Corps that the matter be resolved. Fortunately for me, in late June, 400 persons were taken to a camp at the level of the command of the East Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's go back to the order, please, the order by which you set up the camp, P03240.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you use the -- to organise --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: To organise the camp [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- given his interpretation or testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we please clarify. By "prisoners of war," are you including within that language women and children?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just let --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain this to you so that there should be no dilemma about it. The word "organise" ended up here for the reason that there was a reception centre in Vlasenica in the month of April, not only for the Muslims but for the Serbs as well who had left Gorazde, Tuzla, Kladanj because they were expelled to the municipality of Vlasenica and other municipalities. There were some 3- to 4.000 of them. Now, because it was impossible to put them up in homes, the Vlasenica Crisis Staff decided that they should spend several days there whereupon they would be sent to Serbia and to other municipalities. In addition, not only men but also women and children were put up there who, after the 21st, when the Crisis Staff took up authority, when in a way the TO was established, because they were fearful for their security they asked that the president of the Crisis Staff should provide safe accommodation for --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Wait a moment, please --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- 24 hours before their transfer to Kladanj and elsewhere be arranged. I will wait.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Are you now saying that this camp is a reception centre? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This camp was a reception centre in the month of April, practically until my order was issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we look, please, at paragraph 3 of your order. "The security organ of the battalion in Vlasenica shall conduct operative interviews and shall submit all useful information for control and command to the Birac SV Brigade ..." That's something else that you ordered on the 31st of May; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. This because among prisoners there were armed fighters, unit commanders who had committed criminal offences against the Serb population, and of course the security organ had to send relevant information to the battalion commander and the brigade commander, that's to say me, on the basis of these interviews.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So you'd accept then, wouldn't you, that members of the -- of your brigade and the Vlasenica Battalion took Susica camp detainees away for interrogation, took them out of the camp, yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do accept that the chief of security of the battalion took out individuals - and that wasn't often - singled out those individuals who were relevant for security issues. However, those same persons were taken back. There is no evidence to the effect that this person did not take back to the camp the Muslim or the prisoner of war he had initially taken out.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: The evidence in this case is also that women were removed from the camp and raped. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of it. Let me tell you right away, the brigade command - I'm going back to the heading here - had the task of securing prisoners, that's to say the camp itself. The camp wasn't intended only for the POWs but also for storing material and technical equipment. In military professional terminology, a camp is an area where quarters are organised for troops and for storing materiel and military equipment. A camp doesn't have any specific connotation for anyone. You have "camping" arising out of the word "camp." Mobile and immobile camping. So what we have here is a reception centre, a storage centre for materiel and military equipment, and POWs all at once.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Is it your evidence --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 16 misses the -- the word "connotation" misses negative, there is no negative connotation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that your only concern for POWs, detainees in the camp at Susica and in other detention facilities in Vlasenica, your only concern was for their welfare; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have time to take care of it because of the area of responsibility. As far as the brigade command is concerned, it issued a task to the battalion to provide for the entire camp compound, not just that, for the POWs to make an assessment and that was the role the army had to play. If you see who the commander of the camp was, who the deputy was, who was in charge of security, you will see that it wasn't the army that was involved in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let me ask you about another facility in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to go into private session, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is what this individual says. I'll read it slowly. "During his inspection, Andric approached me." I'll just go to the next paragraph. "Svetozar Andric approached me, pointed with his finger at me and said, 'Why are you so sad'" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Page 4 of the statement in e-court, please. I'm reading from paragraph 19 now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Paragraph 19, and it's going to go all the way down the page. "I replied: 'Comrade Major, I am not sad, I am sick.' "He said: 'I am asking you for a second time: Why are you sad? You are the saddest person here.' "I replied again: 'Comrade Major, I am not sad. I am sick.' "He then asked if someone had beaten us. I told him that nobody had even touched us. Yet I was fully covered in blood-stains, due to the wound I had sustained on my forehead and my broken teeth, and I was wearing a sweater which was stiff from having earlier been soaked in blood, and which then looked like tar. This blood was due to injuries I had received in ..." two villages he names. "He said: 'I know the difference between sorrow and illness. You are sad.' "Svetozar Andric continued to inspect the rows of detainees and I could hear his steps on the wooden floor. The other detainees at that time were in a terrible state, bloodied and beaten. There was not a single detainee without blood traces. After a while, I could hear Svetozar Andric's steps as he approached me again. He said: 'You don't want to tell me why you are sad,' and I replied, 'I told you.'" Going to paragraph 26: "As a result of bad hygienic conditions, we smelled badly so the guards wore masks on their faces. They gave a mask to Andric as well, but he did not use it." Paragraph 28: "I saw Svetozar Andric for a second time ..." just jumping, "about two or three days later a group of Muslim men had recently been transported to the gym. Svetozar Andric again inspected all the detainees and again stopped to speak to me. He said to me, once again: 'You don't want to tell me why you are sad.' I again said: 'I am not sad.'
